                          MAXIMUM PRICES FOR PETROL, DISTILLATE AND
LIGHTING KEROSENE
.1 MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller, by virtue of
the powers conferred by the Prices Regu-
      lation Act 1949, as amended to date, and all other powers me
enabling do hereby make the following Order
under that Act:—

PRICES ORDER No. 122
1. CITATION.
         This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 122.
2. COMMENCEMENT.
         This Order shall come into operation on the date of
publication of this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION.
         The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS.
         In this Order—

2
Papua New Guinea Gazette
No. 4-16th January, 1975
Maximum Prices for Petrol, Distillate and Lighting Kerosene.-
continued
"petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol whether or
not containing additives of any kind;
"distillate" includes any substance normally sold as automotive
distillate whether or not containing additives of
any kind;
"kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene, being a
medium refined petroleum product as
used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether or not
containing additives of any kind;
"wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene means a
person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate
or kerosene for the purpose of resale and not for the purpose of
use;
"supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene, means a
person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate or
kerosene for the purpose of use;
"retail" means for the purpose of consumption or, use.
5. MAXIMUM PRICE.
(i) Support to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied -
(a) at a locality specified in, the first column of Schedule 1 to
this Order; or
(b) at some other place to which the petrol, distillate or kerosene
is transported from any such locality by or
on behalf of a wholesaler or the supplier;
the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of-
(c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the second, third
or fourth column as the case may be, of
Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and
(d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to in
paragraph (b) of this subclause.
(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol, distillate
or kerosene supplied at any one time, cal-
culated in accordance with Subclause (i) of this clause is an amount
involving a fraction of a cent, the supplier
may charge to the next whole cent.
6. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.
Nothing in this Order applies to or in relation to the supply of
petrol, distillate or kerosene to the Govern-
ment, Australia or a Statutory Authority of the Government or
Australia.
7. NOTICES FIXING MAXIMUM PRICES.
Notwithstanding the preceding provisions of this Order, the
Controller may, by notice in writing to any person
or body or association of persons, fix the maximum price at which
petrol, distillate or kerosene may be sold, and
thereupon that maximum price is the price for the purpose of the

                                        MAXIMUM PRICES FOR CIGARETTES

    MILTON FREDIIIUCK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller appointed
under the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as
   amended to date, hereby make the following Order under that Act:-

                                          PRICES ORDER No. 124
1. CITATION.
     This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 124.

2. COMMENCEMENT.

     This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazelle.

3. REVOCATION.
     Prices Order No. 92 is hereby revoked.

4. DEFINITIONS.
     In this Order-

       "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua
New Guinea from imported or locally grown
            tobacco leaf.

       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

     (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be
sold by retail at any of the locations specified

in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and pack spe-
cified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.

Papua New Guinea Gazette


                                            Maximum Prices for
Cigarettes—continued

       (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be
sold by retail at locations other than those

 specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third Column
of Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
 pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.

    6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

       A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order

 applies for sale by retail, or who, offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display
 a ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent

 position in dear and legible figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting such cigarettes, the price at which the
 cigarettes concerned may be bought.

    7. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS.

       Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a notice in
writing is given by the Controller to a supplier of
 cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not
 less than fixed by Clause 4 of this Order, the maximum price at
which cigarettes may be so supplied is the price
 fixed in that Notice.
